headline: Australia bans fully AI-made music from charts and ARIA Awards, effective this Friday
summary: The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) will still allow tracks using generative AI if they are "substantially human made" and raise no manipulation concerns.
details: The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) has announced that any music tracks wholly generated with AI will be ineligible for inclusion on the nation's official music charts. This new rule will also prevent such tracks from winning an ARIA Award.

The updated Code of Practice for the charts, effective this Friday, permits songs that utilize generative AI, but only if the track is "substantially human made" and "raises no stream or chart manipulation concerns."

ARIA CEO Annabelle Herd stated that the charts must remain a transparent measure of music consumption, emphasizing that rewarding unlicensed AI output would undermine the basis of recorded music. She urged radio and other platforms to adopt similar policies supporting human artistry.

This move aligns with a broader push from the global recording industry. Recommendations from the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) in July and calls from major labels like Sony Music, Universal Music Group, and Warner Music Group also advocate for prohibiting fully AI-generated content from charts.

headline_marked: [[Meta's AI agents caused "disruptive actions"]] in internal project to cut staff by 60%
headline: Meta's AI agents caused "disruptive actions" in internal project to cut staff by 60%
summary: A Reuters report reveals Meta's internal "Project OT" aimed to make the company "AI native" by replacing human roles, but faced significant challenges and led to internal disruptions.
details: Meta explored a plan, codenamed "Project OT," to become "AI native" and potentially reduce some teams by up to 60%. This initiative aimed to replace thousands of human roles with AI agents, overseen by smaller human teams.

A Reuters report, based on internal documents and over 20 sources, detailed how Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg initiated Project OT. The plan called for two rounds of layoffs, with the first occurring in May.

Internal documents reviewed by Reuters indicated that AI agents performing daily work made "large-scale, disruptive actions that humans are unlikely to execute," highlighting challenges in AI integration.

Meta confirmed conducting scenario planning exercises to assess the impact of redeployments and role closures, which resulted in moving thousands of employees to priority work. However, not all scenarios were pursued.

The second round of layoffs planned for November was reportedly canceled by Zuckerberg, though the exact reason for the shift was not determined by Reuters. Employee morale was reportedly affected by earlier layoff reports and a paused program tracking keyboard/mouse input for AI training.
Uncertainty about AI's productivity boost also played a role. While internal software code changes were up 220% year-over-year, changes leading to new user features only increased by 36%.
